requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change stops the analyzer from crashing on a [MessagePackObject] type that has duplicate keys or mixes int and string keys. In TypeCollector, after the mixed-key diagnostic is reported the offending member is now skipped with `continue`. The int and string member dictionaries are also guarded with ContainsKey before Add, so a duplicate key no longer throws. Both the property loop and the field loop get the same edits. New analyzer tests check that several diagnostics (MsgPack003/004/005/015) still appear on SuppressSourceGeneration = true types, and that MsgPack011/016/017 do not. New execution tests check that a suppressed type gets no generated formatter but still round-trips. A README section documents the opt-out.
story.why: Issue 2234 says the analyzer stopped working for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types in 3.1.1. The apparent theory is that an exception inside TypeCollector (Dictionary.Add on a duplicate key, or `intKey!.Value` / a null string key on mixed keys) aborts analysis. Nothing in the diff is conditioned on SuppressSourceGeneration, so the fix applies to every MessagePackObject type.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that lists analyzer behaviour, including MsgPack012, which no test covers
Execution tests check run-time serialization and the absence of a generated formatter, not the analyzer
The TypeCollector edits change behaviour for normal (generated) types as well as suppressed ones
story.confidence_overview: High that the crash-avoidance edits in the property loop are exercised by the new duplicate-key and mixed-key tests. The field-loop edits (lines 1148, 1163-1182) are not exercised by any test. Medium-low that this is the actual root cause of issue 2234: the diff never mentions SuppressSourceGeneration in source code. The tests for MsgPack004/015/003 on suppressed types may already have passed before the change.

claims.text: In the property loop, when a member's key kind differs from the earlier members, the analyzer still reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys. It then skips the member with `continue`, instead of reaching `intKey!.Value` with a null int key or building a member from a null string key.
claims.requirement_quote: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true.

breaker.reason: In the property loop, adding `continue;` at line 1008 does prevent reaching `intKey!.Value` at line 1019 when `isIntKey` is true and `intKey` is null, and `MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure` tests that int-then-string case. However, the claim also says `continue;` avoids "building a member from a null string key" in the property loop, which is false: line 1028 is already `else if (stringKey is not null)`, so when `!isIntKey && stringKey == null` the property loop already skipped lines 1029-1043 (unlike the field loop's unguarded `else` at line 1168).

claims.text: README documents that suppressed types are still validated (MsgPack004/005/015/003/012) and are exempt from MsgPack011/016/017. MsgPack005 here covers duplicate keys only, not the mixed-key case. MsgPack012 has no accompanying test.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: In the property loop, adding `continue;` at line 1008 does prevent reaching `intKey!.Value` at line 1019 when `isIntKey` is true and `intKey` is null, and `MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure` tests that int-then-string case. However, the claim also says `continue;` avoids "building a member from a null string key" in the property loop, which is false: line 1028 is already `else if (stringKey is not null)`, so when `!isIntKey && stringKey == null` the property loop already skipped lines 1029-1043 (unlike the field loop's unguarded `else` at line 1168).

Claim C18 disputed: `README.md` line 1627 states `Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).` The phrase "and all of the same kind" explicitly documents the mixed-key case, directly contradicting the claim that "MsgPack005 here covers duplicate keys only, not the mixed-key case."

Nothing in the diff references SuppressSourceGeneration. If issue 2234's root cause is that suppressed types are skipped or filtered before analysis (as opposed to a crash on bad keys), this change does not fix it. The tests for MsgPack004/015/003 on suppressed types may already have passed before the change. The owner should confirm that at least one new test fails on the pre-change code.
The field-loop edits (lines 1148, 1163-1166, 1179-1182) have no test. Every new test uses properties, so duplicate or mixed keys on fields are unverified.

Duplicate-keyed members are now silently dropped instead of throwing. If a user downgrades or suppresses MsgPack005 (for example via .editorconfig), the generator could emit a formatter that omits a member, with no build error.

`continue` skips all later per-member processing for the mismatched member. Any other diagnostics for that member (for example a member-type check, or the formatter attribute handling at 1045) are no longer reported until the key-kind error is fixed.
